title: Completed tensor equivalence for a finite localization
statement:
theorem completion_finite_extension_tensor
    (R : Type u) (S : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [Module.Finite R S] (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] :
    let A := Localization.AtPrime p
    let m := IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A
    let C := AdicCompletion m A
    let B := A ⊗[R] S
    letI := Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra (R := R) (A := A) (B := S)
    let J := p.map (algebraMap R B)
    let Q := p.primesOver S
    let D := fun q : Q ↦
      AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime q.1))
        (Localization.AtPrime q.1)
    letI := Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra (R := R) (A := C) (B := S)
    Nonempty ((C ⊗[R] S) ≃ₐ[S] AdicCompletion J B)

proof.text: Use the explicitly constructed S-algebra map completionFiniteExtensionTensorMap R S p, whose data and algebra laws are proved by quotient-level construction, rather than choosing an unspecified map.

Its bijectivity is the remaining tensor/filtration comparison theorem. Apply AlgEquiv.ofBijective to the constructed map and this bijectivity proof, then wrap the algebra equivalence in Nonempty. This is a decomposition with one remaining lower hole, not a net reduction in holes.

proof_origin.place: Explicit map construction and reduction of Tag 07N9 first equality to bijectivity
